original_test_intent: Update the approved Linux RAID driver/module and controller firmware, restart once and verify exact target versions without storage, kernel, boot or management errors.
original_method: After critical approval, validate signed artifacts, stable controller identity and kernel/initramfs compatibility, execute the vendor sequence under health monitoring, restart once through KVM/OOB and verify the complete boot-to-array path.
manual_activity: User supplies and approves exact Linux artifacts, controller, sequence and recovery; operator supervises flash/restart; agent validates, executes only approved steps and collects evidence.
required_inputs: Signed vendor packages, hashes, updater and exact compatibility/transition documentation
Healthy array, backup, stable power, maintenance window and abort thresholds
KVM/OOB, boot media, rollback/controller recovery and operator
safety_requirements: Bind updater to stable controller identity, not /c0 numbering
Verify signatures, kernel ABI/support, firmware transition and initramfs steps before changes
Require healthy non-rebuilding arrays, stable power and recovery media
Preserve logs; stop on module/package/target ambiguity, updater, initramfs, array, power, boot or kernel error
Never force flash, unload a boot-critical module unsafely, rebuild, auto-rollback or repeatedly restart
agent_execution_scope: Collect module/driver, kernel/initramfs, firmware, controller/array and boot baseline
Validate artifacts and render the exact approved sequence
Execute approved module/package and firmware steps with full output and health monitoring
After one restart verify loaded module, firmware, initramfs/boot, arrays/mounts and logs; do not choose targets or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve target, artifacts, kernel compatibility, sequence and rollback
Supervise firmware/restart and own controller/boot recovery
Review exact pre/post module, firmware, boot and array evidence and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A vendor CLI may flash firmware, but generic /c0 and filename input do not identify the controller or address Linux driver/module installation, initramfs, compatibility and boot recovery.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use vendor-documented Linux package/module and firmware tools bound to stable controller identity, verify/rebuild initramfs only as approved, preserve full output and perform one recovery-supervised restart.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Driver/firmware version check, both updates, restart and source 5/10 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Manage module and firmware updates as one boot-path change with immutable pre/post inventory, guarded initramfs integration and single supervised restart.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds Linux-specific kernel/boot compatibility and exact hardware/artifact provenance without reducing either update.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A firmware-only command cannot substitute for the driver/module step or post-restart kernel evidence.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A module can install successfully yet be absent from the boot initramfs, and controller numbering may change; loaded-module and stable-device evidence are required.

project_override_considerations: DKMS, vendor kmod and in-tree driver paths have different kernel-update behavior; only the approved packaging model may be used for this platform.
expected_evidence: Stable controller identity and pre-update distribution/kernel/module/initramfs/firmware/array state
Full driver/module and firmware updater outputs and exit codes
Initramfs validation plus one-restart KVM/OOB record
Post-update loaded module/version, controller firmware, array/mount/boot health, complete journal/dmesg/syslog/BMC/SEL and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master consistently requires Linux driver and firmware update plus restart; reference differences concern safety completeness only.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Packages, compatibility and recovery are supplyable update prerequisites; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Adds the missing kernel/module/initramfs and stable-controller safeguards to a signed, recoverable firmware update workflow.
independent_technical_reasoning: Linux storage availability after restart depends on the controller firmware, the installed module's kernel compatibility and its inclusion in the boot initramfs. A flash success code alone proves none of these, so the review binds exact hardware and signed artifacts, validates the boot image and requires post-restart loaded-module, mount, array and log evidence.
